newsitem.title: USA: House members urge Clinton to halt new air rule.
newsitem.headline: House members urge Clinton to halt new air rule.

text.p: More than 100 House members Tuesday urged President Clinton on Tuesday to hold off on the administration's proposal to set stricter standards against air pollution.

A letter signed by 114 members -- 36 Democrats and 78 Republicans -- said there was "significant uncertainty surrounding the health benefits, costs and effects" of the Environmental Protection Agency's proposed tighter standards against smog and soot pollution.

About half of the Democrats who signed this letter circulated by Virginia Democrat Rick Boucher also signed an earlier letter with 42 signatures of House Democrats who disputed the need for the proposed new standards.

Boucher in a statement said his letter "demonstrates a strong bi-partisan determination to defer implementation of the new regulations until serious questions regarding the technical basis and scientific justification for the proposed rules can be resolved."
Critics say there has not been enough study on the need for the new rule or its economic consequences, which the EPA disputes.
Health and environmental groups say new standards would prolong thousands of lives annually, and prevent thousands of asthma attacks in children.
But smokestack industries say tougher rules would impose billions of dollars of costs and produce only minor health benefits.

Industrial Midwestern areas, coal-producing areas and areas such as the Southeast that depend on coal-fired electricity have largely oppose the proposal. But it has support in the Northeast and some other regions that would benefit if less air pollution were blown into their areas.

EPA Administrator Carol Browner has said she has not made a final decision on the standards, which she is to announce in July. But she has said studies show that current standards leave many people vulnerable to lung disease.
